kushan-empire.summary: Founded by the Yuezhi from the steppe, it straddled the routes between Rome, Persia, India and China, and under Kanishka carried Buddhism north into Central Asia and on towards China.

gospels.summary: The four accounts of Jesus's life were written between roughly thirty-five and eighty years after his death, in Greek, for communities scattered across the eastern Mediterranean.
gospels.significance: Between thirty-five and eighty years, in a different language from the one Jesus spoke, for communities scattered across the Mediterranean.
gospels.note: Mark is generally dated around 65–75 CE, Matthew and Luke in the 80s, John around 90–110. Traditional attributions to eyewitnesses are held by many Christians and doubted by most critical scholars.

texts.title: Bible and Christian texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

kingdom-of-aksum.summary: A Red Sea trading power that minted its own coinage, raised monumental stelae, and adopted Christianity in the fourth century — among the earliest states anywhere to do so.

moche.summary: Coastal Peruvian society known for irrigation on a large scale and for ceramics of unusual realism, including portrait vessels of identifiable individuals.

ptolemy.summary: Assembled an Earth-centred model of the heavens accurate enough to predict planetary positions, which held authority for fourteen centuries.

marcus-aurelius.summary: Roman emperor whose private notebook of Stoic self-instruction became one of the most read works of ancient philosophy.

nagarjuna.summary: Founder of the Madhyamaka school, arguing that nothing possesses independent existence and that this emptiness is not nihilism but relation.

image.credit: Unknown | Recovered from Himalayan Art Resources

antonine-plague.summary: Carried back by armies returning from the east, it killed millions across the Roman empire and thinned the legions for a generation.
antonine-plague.note: Probably smallpox or measles; contemporary descriptions are not specific enough to settle it.

sogdian-merchants.summary: Merchants from Samarkand and Bukhara ran the commerce of the Silk Road for centuries, and their language became its lingua franca — carrying Buddhist, Manichaean and Christian texts east alongside the goods.

image.credit: A.Davey from Portland, Oregon, EE UU

talmud.summary: Three centuries of rabbinic argument recorded rather than resolved, preserving minority opinions alongside majority rulings — a record of reasoning as much as of conclusions.

texts.title: Judaism texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

three-kingdoms.summary: Sixty years of civil war after the Han collapse, remembered less for its politics than for becoming the subject of one of China's great novels twelve centuries later.

avesta-written.summary: Possibly two thousand years after Zoroaster, the Sasanian empire committed the Avesta to writing — the widest gap between a founder and a written record in this dataset.
avesta-written.note: A script was invented specifically to record it. Much of the canon was subsequently lost; what survives is a fraction of what Sasanian sources describe.

texts.title: Zoroastrian texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

maya-classic.summary: The height of Maya city-states such as Tikal and Palenque, with a fully developed writing system, Long Count calendar and monumental architecture.

ghana-empire.summary: The first of the great West African empires, grown wealthy taxing the trade in gold moving north and salt moving south.
ghana-empire.note: Origins are known mainly from later Arabic geographers; the early dates are inferred.

gupta-empire.summary: A period of consolidation in mathematics, astronomy, Sanskrit literature and temple architecture, often called a classical age of India.
gupta-empire.significance: The period that produced the decimal place-value system. Almost every number written anywhere today descends from the notation formalised here.

kalidasa.summary: The pre-eminent poet and dramatist of classical Sanskrit, whose Shakuntala and Meghaduta set the standard against which later Sanskrit verse was measured — and whose cloud-messenger conceit was still being imitated a thousand years on.
kalidasa.note: One of the wider genuine disputes in Indian literary chronology. Nothing in the works names a patron unambiguously, so the dating rests on language, on astronomical references, and on the tradition placing him at a Gupta court. Proposals run from the first century BCE to the sixth century CE; the bracket holds the Gupta dating most scholars accept.

texts.title: Sanskrit texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

augustine.summary: Fused Christian doctrine with Platonic philosophy and wrote an introspective autobiography unlike anything before it.

hephthalites.summary: Steppe confederation that killed a Sasanian emperor, extracted tribute from Persia, and broke into north-west India, hastening the end of Gupta power.
hephthalites.note: Their origin and language remain unsettled; the sources are hostile and second-hand.

jain-agamas.summary: Close to a millennium after Mahavira, a council in Gujarat set down the Svetambara canon that had until then been carried orally.
jain-agamas.note: The council at Valabhi is dated to either 453 or 466 CE. The Digambara tradition holds that the original canon was lost entirely, and does not accept the Svetambara Agamas — so the gap is disputed in kind, not only in length.

texts.title: Jainism texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

aryabhata.summary: Astronomer-mathematician who gave a place-value system without zero as a symbol, an accurate value of pi, and a heliocentric-leaning account of the Earth's rotation.

tiwanaku.summary: A highland state on Lake Titicaca whose precision stonework at 3,850 metres has attracted more mystical speculation than it deserves and less archaeological attention than it warrants.
